{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25) or recent price declines, as models tend to overreact to short-term volatility.",
    "Apply a mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% to avoid over-optimism.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude after a spike (e.g., >70% above prior peak) by 15-25% to prevent overshoot.",
    "Increase downward bias when history shows persistent downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive days below 65) and sentiment is neutral or negative.",
    "If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply a 5-10% correction factor to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.",
    "When sentiment history includes a 0.33 or higher positive signal, slightly increase forecast by 3-5% to reflect bullish momentum, but cap at 75% above prior peak.",
    "For horizon > 15 days, apply a 10% discount to forecast if recent history shows high volatility or sentiment instability."
  ]
}
